issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of Theorem 4.4, the estimate for $I_2$ bounds the cross term by the global norm $\|z\|_{	ilde{s}}^2$ rather than a localized norm. Summing this bound over all elements $i = 1, \dots, N$ adds the global term $N$ times, producing $N C_* \|z\|_{	ilde{a}}^2 + N C_* \Lambda \|\pi z\|_{\tilde{s}}^2$. Moving this to the left-hand side yields coefficients $C_2 - C_* N$ and $C_2 - C_* \Lambda N$. Here $N = N_{\text{elem}} = \mathcal{O}(H^{-d})$ is the total number of coarse grid elements in $\Omega$. As the coarse mesh is refined ($H \to 0$), $N \to \infty$, which forces both $C_2 - C_* N$ and $C_2 - C_* \Lambda N$ to $-\infty$. Thus $C'' > 0$ cannot hold independently of $N$ (or $H$), and taking the maximum rather than the minimum of the two coefficients cannot yield a lower bound on the sum of norms.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish a localized bound for $I_2$ in terms of local norms on $\hat{K}_i^{m+1}$ whose sum over $i$ is controlled by the finite overlap constant $C_{\text{ol}}$ rather than the global element count $N$.
issues.overall_effect: The exponential decay estimate for the difference between global and localized multiscale basis functions outside oversampling regions is unestablished for refined coarse meshes.
issues.title: Exponential decay estimate fails due to coercive constant depending negatively on total element count
issues.why_classification: Every supported resolution requires a new proof architecture for localizing the Helmholtz perturbation term without accumulating the global element count $N$ as $H \to 0$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
The Fortin trick  suggests that it suffices to check that
\[
\inf_{u\in\tilde{V}} \sup_{ w\in \tilde{V}} \frac{\mathcal{B}(u, w)}{\norm{u}_{\tilde{a}} \norm{w}_{\tilde{a}}}\geq \beta_{\text{glo}}
\]
holds.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Lemma 4.5 exhibits two fatal flaws. First, it asserts $\beta_{\text{cem}} \|u - u_{\text{ms}}\|_{\tilde{a}}^2 \le \mathcal{B}(u - u_{\text{ms}}, u - u_{\text{ms}})$, treating the indefinite, sign-changing Helmholtz sesquilinear form $\mathcal{B}$ as if it were coercive on $V$. Since $\mathcal{B}$ is non-coercive and sign-changing, $\mathcal{B}(w, w)$ can be zero or negative, and $u - u_{\text{ms}} \notin V_{\text{ms}}$, so a discrete inf-sup condition on $V_{\text{ms}}$ cannot justify this step. Second, in attempting to establish the discrete inf-sup stability constant $\beta_{\text{cem}}$, the author bounds $\|v_{\text{ms}} - v_{\text{glo}}\|_{\tilde{a}} \le C_*' H^{-1} \|v_{\text{glo}}\|_{\tilde{a}} = \eta \|v_{\text{glo}}\|_{\tilde{a}}$ while dropping the exponential decay factor $\theta^{(m-1)/2}$. As a result, $\eta = \mathcal{O}(H^{-1})$ blows up as $H \to 0$, contradicting the assumption of small $\eta$ and making $\beta_{\text{cem}} = \beta_{\text{glo}}/4 - 15\alpha\eta/4$ strictly negative for small $H$. Furthermore, the global inf-sup constant $\beta_{\text{glo}}$ used here was never proven, based only on the false assertion that the Fortin trick allows reducing inf-sup on $V_{\text{glo}}$ to inf-sup on the orthogonal subspace $\tilde{V}$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish a valid discrete inf-sup condition on $V_{\text{glo}}$, retain the exponential decay factor $\theta^{(m-1)/2}$ in $\eta$ with an oversampling layer $m = \mathcal{O}(|\log H|)$ so that $\beta_{\text{cem}} > 0$, and prove an error bound using Babuska's inf-sup framework rather than falsely invoking coercivity of $\mathcal{B}$ on $u - u_{\text{ms}}$.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete inf-sup stability of the multiscale formulation, Cea's lemma, and the main a priori error estimate for the CEM-GMsFEM multiscale solution (Theorem 4.6) are unproven and invalid.
issues.title: Invalid assertion of coercivity for indefinite Helmholtz problem and blowup of inf-sup perturbation parameter in Cea's Lemma
issues.why_classification: The primary claim and its main convergence theorem (Theorem 4.6) are invalidated. Repairing them requires establishing discrete inf-sup stability and a non-coercive quasi-optimality theory for the multiscale space, which requires essentially new proof architecture.
